senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; preced. wds.) silver; (sub. מעה) a silver piece, M’ah (one sixth of a Denar, v. Zuckerm. Jüd. Münz. p. 15; p. 33, note 203); in gen. money, value.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 1:1">Kidd. I, 1</cite> <he>בכ׳</he> by (handing to her) an object of value.
<cite ref="Yevamot 63b:7">Yeb. 63ᵇ</cite> <he>שמזונותיו תלויין בכַסְפּוֹ</he> whose livelihood depends on his money (a money-lender).

<cite ref="Mishnah Shevuot 6:1">Shebu. VI, 1</cite> <he>הטענה שתי כ׳</he> the claim must amount to no less than two M’ah. Tosef. Keth. XIII (XII), 3 <he>כ׳ בבל</he> the Babylonian silver standard; <he>כ׳ א״י</he> the Palestinean &c.

Ib. כ׳ שדיברה … זו היא כ׳ צורי זה ירושלמי wherever the Torah speaks of Kesef (as fines), it must be paid according to the Tyrian standard … that is the Jerusalem kesef (eight times the provincial kesef כ׳ מדינה, v. Zuckerm. l. c.); a. v. fr.—Pl. כְּסָפִים.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 42a:6">B. Mets. 42ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Pesachim 31b:9">Pes. 31ᵇ</cite> <he>כ׳ אין להם שמירה וכ׳</he> coins given in trust are not duly guarded unless they are buried in the ground.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 4:1:3">Y. Yoma IV, beg. 41ᵇ</cite> <he>בשלשה … ובכ׳</he> by three methods was the land of Israel divided, by lots, by the Urim and Tummim, and according to the value of property; a. e.
